prompt: Someone on the platform team ran a deployments import from Settings yesterday and it says it only partly worked. What went wrong?
final_text:
Most of it worked. Priya Raman's deployments import (submitted 2026-10-16 at 14:22 UTC) loaded **45 of its 48 rows**. 3 rows were refused. This import handles each row on its own, so those 3 didn't stop the others from going in.

**The 3 refused rows:**

| Row | ImportId | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| 32 | dep-031 | No environment named `qa-west` |
| 33 | dep-032 | No environment named `qa-west` |
| 45 | dep-044 | No version with id `0b2d4f6a-8c9e-4f1a-b2c3-d4e5f6a7b8c9` |

**Causes:**
- **`qa-west` isn't a Wayd environment.** The only environments, active or retired, are `qa-east` (Testing), `stg-us` (Staging) and `prd-us` (Production). Either the file has a typo for `qa-east`, or `qa-west` really exists in their pipeline and was never set up in Wayd.
- **The version id on dep-044 doesn't match any version.** I looked it up and got "not found". It may have been copied wrong, or the version may never have been recorded (or may have been deleted).

**How to fix it:**
1. For dep-031 and dep-032: if `qa-west` is real, someone needs to create it first, with the right category and ring order. If it was meant to be `qa-east`, correct the file.
2. For dep-044: find the correct version id. If that version isn't in Wayd yet, record it first.
3. Then import **only those 3 rows** again, as a new file. Deployments have no unique key to spot duplicates, so re-sending the whole file would create the other 45 a second time. Retrying the refused rows on the existing run won't work either, because it resends them exactly as submitted, typos included.

If you can tell me whether `qa-west` is a real environment and what dep-044 was meant to point at, I can prepare the corrected 3-row file and check it before anything is imported.

prompt: How has Falcon (FALC) been doing on velocity and say/do over its recent sprints? I'm trying to decide how much to commit for next sprint.
final_text:
Falcon finishes roughly **32 story points per sprint**, but it only completes about **79% of what it commits to**. It has been committing more than it finishes.

**Six sprints counted** (2026.18 to 2026.24, Jul 8 to Oct 13). The org's default window is 6. Sprint 2026.23 IP was left out because it's an innovation and planning sprint, which isn't comparable.

| Measure | Average | Range | Std dev |
|---|---|---|---|
| Velocity (story points) | 31.8 | 21 – 40 | 6.5 |
| Velocity (work items) | 10.5 | 8 – 13 | 1.7 |
| Predictability (points) | 88% | 65% – 100% | 13% |
| Say/do (points) | 79% | 57% – 94% | 13% |

Sprint by sprint (most recent first):

| Sprint | Points done | Predictability | Say/do |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026.24 | 34 | 95% | 85% |
| 2026.22 | 27 | 78% | 66% |
| 2026.21 | 38 | 100% | 92% |
| 2026.20 | 21 | 65% | 57% |
| 2026.19 | 31 | 89% | 80% |
| 2026.18 | 40 | 100% | 94% |

**What this means for planning:**
- **There's a 2:1 spread in output** (21 to 40 points), so the average is only a rough guide. Use a range, not one number.
- **Say/do is lower than predictability, by about 9 points.** Some work added mid-sprint gets finished instead of committed items. When predictability hits 100% (2026.18 and .21), it's partly because added work made up for committed items that weren't done.
- **They commit about 35 points a sprint.** I worked this out as velocity ÷ predictability, so it's approximate, and a floor in the 100% sprints because predictability is capped there. At 35 points, about 1 in 5 committed points doesn't get done.
- **2026.24 was a good sprint** (34 points, 85% say/do), but one sprint isn't a trend.

**My suggestion: commit about 28–32 story points (around 9–10 items).** That's at or a little below the median velocity (about 32.5) and below what they usually commit. That should push say/do toward 85–90% without leaving them underloaded. If they finish early, they can pull in more work, and that counts toward velocity without hurting say/do. Adjust down if the next sprint has less capacity (holidays, people out) or a lot of unplanned work coming in. The two weakest sprints (21 and 27 points) might have had a cause like that, and it's worth checking before you set the number.

prompt: Where did the Raptors put their effort between July 1 and September 30, 2026? Break it down by project.
final_text:
Between 1 July and 30 September 2026, about a third of the Raptors' completed work was not linked to any project. The rest went to four projects, all in the **Digital Commerce** portfolio. Mobile Experience Refresh took the largest share.

**How this is measured:** The Raptors (Falcon, Osprey and Kestrel) finished 412 user stories and bugs in that period. Epics and features aren't counted. Each team's share is weighed in its own sizing unit and the teams are combined by share of items finished, because adding story points across teams with different estimating scales would mislead. Items with no estimate were left out of the weighting: 248 of the 271 items from point-sized teams had one.

| Project | Share of effort | Items | Team that did the most |
|---|---|---|---|
| **No project** | **32.7%** | 135 | Kestrel (82 items) |
| Mobile Experience Refresh (MOBX) | 26.4% | 109 | Osprey (87 items) |
| Payments Reconciliation (PAYRC) | 18.9% | 78 | Kestrel (62 items) |
| Self-Service Onboarding (ONBRD) | 15.2% | 63 | Falcon (50 items) |
| Billing Export Retirement (BILLX) | 6.8% | 28 | Falcon (22 items) |

**What stands out:**

- **A third of the work isn't linked to a project.** Neither the 135 items nor their parent items link to a project. That is well above the roughly 20–30% where it starts to matter, so this much effort doesn't show up in the portfolio.
- **Kestrel accounts for most of that gap.** 82 of its 141 items (about 58%) have no project. It's worth asking Kestrel whether this is support or maintenance work, or project work that was never linked.
- **Each project has a clear main team.** Osprey did about 80% of the Mobile Experience Refresh items, Kestrel about 80% of Payments Reconciliation, and Falcon about 80% of both Self-Service Onboarding and Billing Export Retirement.
- **The three teams finished similar amounts.** Falcon and Kestrel each finished 141 items and Osprey finished 130, so each delivered about a third.
- None of the four projects is in a program.

prompt: Is Osprey's backlog in good enough shape to plan the next PI from? Mostly I want to know how many weeks of runway they have.
final_text:
I can't give you a reliable runway number. Wayd won't calculate one for Osprey because the team doesn't have enough history: it finished **7 work items in the last 90 days** (Jul 19 – Oct 16), and the Runway check needs at least 10. That shortfall is the main thing to know before you plan the next PI from this backlog.

I tried again with a 180-day history window, but the response still came back with 90 days and the same results, so the longer window wasn't used. It would be worth trying again or checking in Wayd itself.

**A rough estimate, not Wayd's figure:** 7 finished items in about 13 weeks is roughly 0.5 items a week. There are 18 open items, so that works out to something like **30+ weeks**. That's past the 26-week point where Wayd would flag a backlog as too long. Treat it as very soft: it's based on 7 data points, it counts items rather than points, and over a quarter of the items have no estimate.

**Backlog shape** (18 open items: 6 in progress, 12 not started; 39 story points estimated):

| Check | Result | Items |
|---|---|---|
| Missing Estimate | **Unhealthy**, 5 of 18 (28%) | MOB-232, MOB-234, MOB-236, MOB-239, MOB-242 |
| Net Flow | **At Risk**, 1.29 | 9 created vs 7 finished, so the backlog is growing |
| Stale | **At Risk**, 3 of 18 | MOB-237, MOB-241, MOB-244 (unchanged since June 30) |
| No Parent | **At Risk**, 2 of 18 | MOB-234, MOB-244 |
| No Project | Healthy, 1 of 18 | MOB-241 |
| WIP Load | Healthy, 1.0 per member | but see below |
| Aging WIP, Oversized | Not assessed (not enough history) | |

These grades use Wayd's default thresholds.

**Something the grades hide:** all 6 in-progress items (MOB-230 to MOB-235) are assigned to **Marcus Hale**, and all were started on Oct 5. WIP Load shows as Healthy only because it averages across the 6 team members. In practice one person is carrying all the work in progress, which may also explain why so little has been finished.

**My take: it isn't ready for PI planning yet.** Before planning:
1. Estimate the 5 unestimated items. Two of them, MOB-232 and MOB-234, are already in progress.
2. Decide whether the 3 stale items (MOB-237, MOB-241, MOB-244) are still wanted. If so, give MOB-241 a project and MOB-244 a parent; MOB-234 needs a parent too.
3. Look at why Marcus has all 6 items in progress.
4. Plan capacity from sprint velocity rather than backlog runway. I can pull Osprey's velocity, predictability and say/do over its recent sprints if that would help.
